userStories.notes:
Models can now be downloaded through the API: `GET /models`, `GET /models/{id}`, `POST /models/{id}/download` and `POST /models/{id}/cancel`. A background thread in the API process downloads only the revision-pinned files and follows redirects only to `*.huggingface.co` and `*.hf.co` over https. It resumes a partial `.part` file with an HTTP Range request, stores progress in SQLite, and checks each file's SHA-256. A wrong file is deleted and the model becomes `failed` with a readable message. API startup resumes any model left `downloading` or `verifying`. The Apache 2.0 text is copied to `/data/models/<model>/LICENSE.txt`, and the license name and link are in every state response. `NARRASTEP_LOCAL_GENERATION=disabled` returns 403 `LOCAL_GENERATION_DISABLED` before any network access. - No other `.env` key is needed.

userStories.title: Start and stop the llama.cpp server for a generation
userStories.description: The worker starts `llama-server` on 127.0.0.1 in its container, waits for health, sends requests and stops it.
acceptanceCriteria: Safe argument arrays and `llama_server_environment`, with a loopback address only
Tests with a stand-in server cover start, a failed health check, a request failure, and that the process is always stopped
A memory check before the job gives a readable `GENERATION_OUT_OF_MEMORY` error (K5), translated into Italian
userStories.notes:
I added `backend/app/services/llama_session.py`, which can start the pinned `llama-server` on 127.0.0.1, wait for health, send a request and always stop it. It also checks memory first and raises `GENERATION_OUT_OF_MEMORY`, now translated into Italian. It has only run against a stand-in script, because the real server and a model were never started. No job or route calls it yet; P06.3d is meant to. `check.sh backend` (format, lint, types, full tests, OpenAPI), `check.sh docs` and `check.sh web` all passed. I did not run e2e or desktop.

- **Start, health and requests:** the command is an argument array with a fixed `--host 127.0.0.1` and a free loopback port, and no host parameter exists. It runs with `shell=False` and `llama_server_environment`, and server output is discarded. `GET /health` is polled until 200. Requests to `/v1/chat/completions` ignore proxy variables. A server error, a timeout, a dead server or an empty answer raises `LlamaServerRequestError`, and its message never includes the response body.
- **Stop:** `LlamaServerSession` is a context manager that terminates the process, waits, then kills it. A failed health check or an early exit stops the process before the error leaves `start()`. Stopping twice, or before a start, is safe.
- **Memory check (K5):** I chose the cgroup v2 headroom (`memory.max` minus `memory.current` less `inactive_file`) combined with `/proc/meminfo` `MemAvailable`, taking the smaller. Required memory is the model files plus a 1 GiB overhead. Paths are parameters so tests can supply files. If neither source is readable, the check passes with a warning. This is documented in `LOCAL_GENERATION.md`.
- **Italian text:** `GENERATION_OUT_OF_MEMORY` is added to `error-text.ts`, `messages.en.json`, `messages.it.json`, `catalogs.spec.ts` and `italian.spec.ts`.
- **Tests:** `backend/tests/test_llama_session.py` has 30 tests, covering start, a failed health check, an early exit, a request failure, a timeout, a kill after ignored termination, and the memory check.
- **Docs:** I updated `LOCAL_GENERATION.md`, `ARCHITECTURE.md`, `API.md`, `STATUS.md` and the dated progress line under P06.3 in `ROADMAP.md`. The P06.3c claim on that line is left for the orchestrator to tick.

Checks passed: `check.sh docs` (links valid) and `check.sh backend` (format, lint, types, tests, OpenAPI current). I ran the new test file on its own earlier: it passed, and I did not note the count. The script installs the model through the API (download, wait, enable) and builds 10-minute and 60-minute `meeting` projects from a repeated FFmpeg flite clip. It uploads and processes each project untimed, then times only the generation. A run still going at 45 minutes is cancelled and reported as `outcome=cut`, and `--limit-minutes` can only lower that. It prints numbers and fixed words only, and applies the Default model rule (60-minute run in at most 1800 s, peak memory under 6 GiB). A cut, failed or missing 60-minute run never passes, and E2B prints `not_applicable`. Peak memory is an estimate. The model server runs in the worker container, so the script samples /proc/meminfo in the api container. That file shows the whole Docker VM, which includes the worker. The estimate counts mapped pages, because llama-server maps its weights as file pages. The reported peak is the highest sample minus the baseline taken before queueing, at 2-second resolution. I did not compare it with a cgroup reading. ROADMAP P06.5 stays unchecked.
